precepts.text: When he shall roar, then the children shall tremble from the west. How did they get to the west? Deuteronomy 33:17 and 2 Esdras 13 just told you.
precepts.point: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors: what God promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was not yet fulfilled in their day, but Joseph ruled all Egypt. Canaan wasn't ours yet, and Joseph already had the crown.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“They shall walk after the Lord: he shall roar like a lion: when he shall roar, then the children shall tremble from the west.” The children of Israel are in the west when the Lord roars.

How did they get to the west? Deuteronomy 33:17 and 2 Esdras 13 just told you. Ephraim and Manasseh, with the horns of the unicorn, pushed the people together to the ends of the earth, and the ten tribes went a year and a half's journey into the region called Arsareth.

So the blessing of Joseph in Genesis 49, “in the last days,” is a blessing on a people in the western hemisphere, by the waters, on the islands. It is from the west that the children will tremble and come when the Lord roars.

precepts.text: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west.
precepts.point: When the Lord shall roar like a lion, the children shall tremble from the west, the western hemisphere where the tribes are primarily scattered.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
Hosea says the Lord “shall roar like a lion: when he shall roar, then the children shall tremble from the west.” The west is the western hemisphere, where the tribes are primarily scattered.

Isaiah says the same: “Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west”. The Lord gathers his children from where they are, and the west is where most of them are, here in America and this side of the world.

So when the Lord roars, the children who tremble and walk after him come from the west, and he gathers them. That is the hope for the tribes over here, but it comes with a warning. Before this the class read that Babylon's “sins have reached unto heaven”, and that we must come out of the ways of America and out of her idolatry. If we don't repent of our stubbornness, our bullheadedness and our idolatry, we will get the same judgment as her. The seed that is gathered from the west is the seed that answers the roar and walks after the Lord.

precepts.text: I will save my people from the east country and from the west country and bring them to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, as the encyclopedia itself says we remain here until the time of restoration.
precepts.point: When the Lord shall roar like a lion, the children shall tremble from the west, the western hemisphere where the tribes are primarily scattered.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country”. The children who tremble from the west in Hosea are the ones the Lord saves from the west country. “And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.”

Remember what the Jewish Encyclopedia said earlier in the class about Arzareth: the land beyond the great river, far from the habitation of man, where the ten tribes of Israel would dwell observing the laws of Moses until the time of the restoration, and Columbus identified America with that land. It was prophesied that we would be over here until the time of restoration. This is that restoration: the Lord bringing us from the west country to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem.

And it is “in truth and in righteousness”. That is why the class closed on idolatry: “the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil”, and our stubbornness and disdain for God's commandments are idolatry. Flee from idolatry, so that you are among the people he brings back.

precepts.text: When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion.
precepts.point: When he roars, the children shall tremble from the west, and he will place them in their houses.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel?” God is saying, how am I going to turn away from you, my son, and deliver you forever to the heathen? Admah and Zeboim were the cities round about Sodom and Gomorrah that were utterly destroyed, and he cannot do that to us. Though he strikes us with righteous judgment in these curses, he has not forgotten us. “I will not execute the fierceness of mine anger”: all the horror of these curses we deal with is mercy.

What comes after the repentance is the honor, and Zechariah shows it: “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”, that is, repent, and “even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”. Then: “When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man.”

This is talking about a weapon. Judah is bent first, like the bow, and then he fills the bow with Ephraim, like an arrow. It is the same order as Hosea 11:10: he roars like a lion because the tents of Judah are raised first, and the northern kingdom sees that example and follows it, and the children tremble from the west, from the western hemisphere. Thy sons, O Greece, goes into Edom, Esau, Cain, all these countries that rule with a fist of iron.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning”. That arrow is us. Christ leads the charge, and we get to move like that too, with the two-edged sword in our hand to execute vengeance upon the heathen, the honor all his saints have. “they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine; and they shall be filled like bowls, and as the corners of the altar”: we partake in the vengeance, like the blood of the sacrifice filling the bowls thrown on the altar. We don't just stand by and watch it.

So we don't fight physically now; we repent now and fight through preaching, and God fights for us later. He will place us in our houses, tell us, you're from Asher, you're from Ephraim, from Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, Naphtali, and give us back our royal heritage and our identity.

precepts.text: The Assyrian shall be their king because they refused to return, and the sword shall abide on their cities.
precepts.point: She became famous among women, for judgment was executed upon her, the way everybody knows when a woman has been run through. Everybody knew the northern kingdom was gone.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Because she doted on them, “I have delivered her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Assyrians”. Hosea says the same of Ephraim: “He shall not return into the land of Egypt, but the Assyrian shall be his king, because they refused to return.”

The lover she doted on became her master. The Assyrian shall be their king because they refused to return to the Most High, and the sword abides on their cities. So the Assyrians “discovered her nakedness: they took her sons and her daughters, and slew her with the sword”.

precepts.text: Israel is called the Most High's son, even his firstborn.
precepts.point: When Israel was a child, then the Most High loved him, and called his son out of Egypt.

note.label: Hosea 11: When Israel Was a Child

precepts.why: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.” Israel is the Most High’s son. Moses was told to say to Pharaoh, “Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn”. The son called out of Egypt is Israel, his firstborn, whom he loved when Israel was a child.

precepts.text: The Lord is in the midst of Israel and there is none else.
precepts.point: He will not execute the fierceness of his anger, for he is God and not man, the Holy One in the midst of thee.

note.label: Hosea 11: When Israel Was a Child

precepts.why:
The Most High asks “How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel?” His heart is turned within him, his repentings are kindled together, and he will not execute the fierceness of his anger, “for I am God, and not man; the Holy One in the midst of thee”.

Joel says the same of him: “ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.” The Lord is in the midst of Israel and there is none else. That is why he does not return to destroy Ephraim: he is God and not man, the Holy One in the midst of his people.

precepts.text: The prophecy quoted: when Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
precepts.point: They remain in Egypt until the death of Herod, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, Out of Egypt have I called my son.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
They stayed in Egypt until the death of Herod, “that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son.”

The prophet is Hosea: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.” When it was first spoken, the son called out of Egypt was Israel, when Israel was a child. Christ went down into Egypt and was called out of it as Israel was, and Matthew says that word was fulfilled in him. The son out of Egypt is Israel, and the son out of Egypt is Christ.
